profile.heading: Technical evidence for {{framework}}
profile.scope_state: `{{name}}`, cumulative findings registry; see the original runs for coverage.
profile.scope_image: `{{name}}`, image `{{reference}}` read from the registry; point-in-time static analysis.

profile.frequency_run: Frequency and observation period: a single run; it doesn't show continuous operation of the control.

profile.matrix_note: The matrix is a preparation guide; it doesn't assess control effectiveness or replace the auditor's judgment.

audit.deadlines_body: Workspace policy: {{policy}}, counted from first detection. They apply to open or in-progress findings; fixed findings and approved exceptions don't expire. With a deadline running: {{running}}; overdue: {{overdue}} across {{actions}}; due in the next 7 days: {{soon}}.
audit.deadlines_truncated: Listing the {{limit}} most overdue actions out of {{total}}; all of them are in the findings table.
audit.deadlines_included: Remediation deadlines are in the “Remediation deadlines” section of this report.
audit.deadlines_missing: This report doesn't include remediation deadlines: generate it from the repository's current state (Findings → Current state) to include them.
audit.controls_note: The link to each control is indicative: the auditor assesses the control's effectiveness together with the rest of the team's documentation (policy, owners, frequency and samples from the period).
audit.summary: {{findings}} in the scope of this report: {{critical}}, {{high}}, {{medium}} and {{low}}. Open or in progress: {{active}}; fixed: {{fixed}}; with an approved exception: {{excepted}}.

audit.summary_kev_other: {{count}} of the open findings have known active exploitation (CISA KEV).
audit.summary_grouped: They group into {{actions}}: advisories on the same dependency are closed by a single update.
audit.method_static: Static analysis of {{date}}, without running the code or sending it to external services.
audit.method_state: Cumulative state of the repository as of {{date}}: it combines full scans and pull request reviews, with the date each finding was detected and, where relevant, fixed.
audit.method_gaps: Not fully completed: {{gaps}}. Those areas don't mean “no findings”.
audit.no_findings: No findings in the chosen scope.
audit.no_exceptions_scope: No accepted risks or false positives declared in scope.
audit.no_exceptions: No accepted risks or false positives declared.

audit.coverage_incomplete: Scanned, but none complete (an engine didn't run): {{list}}.

audit.portfolio_method_state: Each repository's state combines its full scans and pull request reviews: a finding is marked fixed when it stops appearing in a full scan, never because of an incomplete one.
audit.open_truncated: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} actions; the full detail is in each repository's report.
audit.no_open: No open critical or high findings.
audit.period_note: Findings detected up to {{end}} and not fixed before {{start}}. Their status and deadlines are as of {{issued}}.
audit.summary_scan: {{findings}} in the scope of this report: {{critical}}, {{high}}, {{medium}} and {{low}}. Open or in progress: {{active}}; with an approved exception: {{excepted}}.

cc3_2.name: Risk identification and analysis
cc3_2.text: Findings prioritized by severity, active exploitation (CISA KEV) and likelihood (EPSS).

cc7_1.name: Detection of vulnerabilities and misconfigurations
cc7_1.text: Analysis of code, dependencies, secrets and infrastructure, with its engines and coverage.

cc8_1.name: Change management
cc8_1.text: Review of what each change introduces before it's merged, when used on pull requests or in CI.

a8_8.name: Management of technical vulnerabilities
a8_8.text: Vulnerabilities identified, assessed and under treatment, with their status.

a8_9.name: Configuration management
a8_9.text: Review of infrastructure as code, containers and pipelines.

a8_28.name: Secure coding
a8_28.text: Static analysis of in-house code and secret detection.

a8_29.name: Security testing in development
a8_29.text: Automated security tests built into the development lifecycle.

r6_2_4.name: Prevent common software attacks
r6_2_4.text: Static analysis of in-house code against injection, XSS, deserialization and other common flaws.

r6_3_1.name: Identify vulnerabilities and rank their risk
r6_3_1.text: Findings with severity, active exploitation (CISA KEV) and likelihood (EPSS).

r6_3_2.name: Inventory of software and its components
r6_3_2.text: Dependency inventory exportable as an SBOM (CycloneDX) from every scan.

r6_3_3.name: Critical patches within one month
r6_3_3.text: Remediation deadlines by severity and overdue findings.

annex_i_ii_1.name: Identify and document vulnerabilities and components
annex_i_ii_1.text: Findings per scan and a component inventory exportable as a CycloneDX SBOM.

annex_i_ii_2.name: Address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay
annex_i_ii_2.text: Status of each vulnerability, recommended action and remediation deadlines.

annex_i_ii_3.name: Regular security testing and reviews
annex_i_ii_3.text: Automated scans on every change and on the main branch, with their coverage.

art_14.name: Report actively exploited vulnerabilities
art_14.text: Input: vulnerabilities from the CISA KEV catalog flagged as actively exploited. The record of notifications is in Pitangus's Compliance view.

vulnerabilities.name: Ongoing prevention and treatment of vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.text: Findings identified and prioritized, with their status and remediation deadline.

testing.name: Security testing and action plan
testing.text: Automated scans with their coverage; recommended actions per finding.

traceability.name: Traceability of decisions
traceability.text: Exceptions and decisions with reason, owner, date and expiry.

risk.name: Measures to prevent incidents
risk.text: Software vulnerabilities identified and prioritized by risk and active exploitation.

improvement.name: Periodic security review
improvement.text: Scans on every change and of the main branch, with their coverage and remediation deadlines.

evidence.name: Record of measures and decisions
evidence.text: Triage decisions with reason, owner and date, kept as history.

vulnerabilities.name: Management of technical vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.text: Vulnerabilities in code, dependencies and images with severity, status and deadline.

secure_development.name: Security in the development lifecycle
secure_development.text: Review of what each change introduces before it's merged, and scans of the main branch.

evidence.name: Record for supervision
evidence.text: Report with scope, method, coverage and decisions, ready for review.

art21_2_d.name: Supply chain security
art21_2_d.text: Inventory of third-party components (CycloneDX SBOM) with their known vulnerabilities, as input to assess what suppliers deliver.

art21_2_e.name: Security in acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure
art21_2_e.text: Vulnerabilities found in code, dependencies, IaC and images, with status, triage decision and remediation deadline.

art21_2_f.name: Policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures
art21_2_f.text: Measurable record of the period: scan coverage, open versus fixed findings and deadline compliance.

ir_6_2.name: Secure development life cycle
ir_6_2.text: Security testing built into development: each change is analyzed before it is merged when used on pull requests or CI, and so is the main branch.

ir_6_5.name: Security testing
ir_6_5.text: Type, scope, date and results of each test, with the criticality and mitigating action of each finding (6.5.2(c)).

ir_6_10.name: Vulnerability handling and disclosure
ir_6_10.text: Recorded scan results (6.10.2(b)), deadlines for critical issues (6.10.2(c)) and the documented reason when a vulnerability is not fixed (6.10.3: triage and OpenVEX). The annex binds only the entities its Article 1 lists; for the rest it is a reference.

art_8_2.name: Identification
art_8_2.text: Continuous identification of ICT vulnerabilities in the entity's own software, its dependencies and its images.

art_9_4_e.name: Protection and prevention (ICT change management)
art_9_4_e.text: Security assessment recorded for each change before it is merged, when used on pull requests or CI.

art_24_5.name: General requirements for the performance of digital operational resilience testing
art_24_5.text: Prioritization, classification and remediation status of every finding the tests revealed, with deadlines.

art_25_1.name: Testing of ICT tools and systems
art_25_1.text: Results of vulnerability assessments and scans and of source code reviews, two of the tests Article 25(1) lists.

rts_10_2.name: Vulnerability and patch management
rts_10_2.text: Automated scanning, tracking of third-party and open-source libraries, prioritization and a record of each vulnerability until it is resolved (points (b), (d), (f), (g) and (h)). The weekly frequency required for assets that support critical or important functions depends on how often you scan.

rts_16_3.name: ICT systems acquisition, development, and maintenance
rts_16_3.text: Static source code review that identifies vulnerabilities, and the follow-up of their correction. The dynamic testing the article also requires is not part of this evidence.

art_32_1_b.name: Security of processing: ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience
art_32_1_b.text: Vulnerabilities in the software that processes personal data, with status and remediation deadline.

art_32_1_d.name: Security of processing: regularly testing, assessing and evaluating effectiveness
art_32_1_d.text: Regular automated security testing of the application, with its coverage and results over the period.

po_3.name: Implement Supporting Toolchains
po_3.text: Artifacts the toolchain generates as evidence of secure development practices (task PO.3.3).

ps_3.name: Archive and Protect Each Software Release
ps_3.text: Provenance of the components of each analyzed version, shared as an SBOM (task PS.3.2).

pw_4.name: Reuse Existing, Well-Secured Software When Feasible Instead of Duplicating Functionality
pw_4.text: Ongoing check of third-party and open-source components for known vulnerabilities (task PW.4.4).

pw_7.name: Review and/or Analyze Human-Readable Code to Identify Vulnerabilities and Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
pw_7.text: Code analysis of every change, with each issue recorded and triaged in the workflow (task PW.7.2).

rv_1.name: Identify and Confirm Vulnerabilities on an Ongoing Basis
rv_1.text: Continuous analysis of code, dependencies and images to detect new vulnerabilities (tasks RV.1.1 and RV.1.2).

rv_2.name: Assess, Prioritize, and Remediate Vulnerabilities
rv_2.text: Severity, risk decision (fix, accept with owner and expiry, or not affected) and deadline for each vulnerability (tasks RV.2.1 and RV.2.2).

id_am_02.name: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
id_am_02.text: Component inventory per repository and image, exportable as a CycloneDX SBOM.

id_ra_01.name: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
id_ra_01.text: Vulnerabilities identified by the scans, recorded one by one and validated when they are reviewed in triage.

id_ra_06.name: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
id_ra_06.text: The response chosen for each vulnerability, with priority, deadline and the follow-up of its status.

id_ra_07.name: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
id_ra_07.text: Security review of each change, and exceptions recorded with reason, owner and expiry.

pr_ps_06.name: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
pr_ps_06.text: Automated security checks built into the life cycle, with their coverage and results.

ra_5.name: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
ra_5.text: Scans of code, dependencies and images, analysis of the results, and tracking of remediation against its deadlines (RA-5 a, c, d).

si_2.name: Flaw Remediation
si_2.text: Flaws identified and reported, with the time allowed to correct each one (SI-2 a, c).

sa_11.name: Developer Testing and Evaluation
sa_11.text: Security testing during development, including static code analysis (SA-11(1)), and the correction of the flaws found.

cm_3.name: Configuration Change Control
cm_3.text: Security impact analysis of each proposed change before it is merged (CM-3 b).

cm_8.name: System Component Inventory
cm_8.text: Software component inventory per repository and image (SBOM).

risk_analysis.name: Risk analysis (Required)
risk_analysis.text: Input to the risk analysis: technical vulnerabilities in the applications that handle ePHI, with their severity. The analysis HIPAA requires covers far more than code.

risk_management.name: Risk management (Required)
risk_management.text: Measures taken against each vulnerability (fixed, or accepted risk with its reason) and their deadlines.

evaluation.name: Evaluation
evaluation.text: Periodic technical evidence of application security, as part of the evaluation.

art_168b11_iii.name: Security throughout the life cycle, including vulnerability tests and code analysis before production
art_168b11_iii.text: Analysis of the code and its dependencies on each change before it is merged (on pull requests or CI), as part of the testing before production.

art_168b11_ix.name: Corrective actions or compensating controls for detected vulnerabilities, by risk level
art_168b11_ix.text: Corrective action or accepted risk for each vulnerability, according to its severity.

art_168b12_v.name: Classification of detected vulnerabilities
art_168b12_v.text: Classification of each vulnerability by severity, to apply the institution's own methodology.

art_168b12_vi_vii.name: Remediation plans and their follow-up
art_168b12_vi_vii.text: Owner, deadline and status of each finding to fix, for the remediation plan and its follow-up. The infrastructure scanning calendar, the external pentests and the filing with the CNBV are outside this evidence.

art_63_iii.name: Security throughout the life cycle, including vulnerability tests and code analysis before production
art_63_iii.text: Analysis of the code and its dependencies on each change before it is merged (on pull requests or CI), as part of the testing before production.

art_63_ix.name: Corrective actions or compensating controls for detected vulnerabilities
art_63_ix.text: Corrective action or accepted risk for each vulnerability, according to its severity.

art_64_v.name: Classification of detected vulnerabilities
art_64_v.text: Classification of each vulnerability by severity, to apply the institution's own methodology.

art_64_vi_vii.name: Remediation plans and their follow-up
art_64_vi_vii.text: Owner, deadline and status of each finding, and the later scan that shows it fixed, as support for the follow-up. The bimonthly infrastructure scanning is outside this evidence.

art_21.name: Vulnerability scanning and remediation plan
art_21.text: Scan results for code and images, critical and high findings with their remediation deadline, and the data for the remediation plan. The bimonthly scan of the whole infrastructure is outside this evidence.

art_28_i.name: Vulnerability tests and code analysis before release; change control
art_28_i.text: Analysis of the code and its dependencies before each change is merged, with a record of the review.

art_18.name: Administrative, technical and physical security measures
art_18.text: Technical evidence of the security measures of the software that processes personal data: vulnerabilities, status and remediation.
